RUBIO, MERKLEY ON UYGHUR FORCED LABOR PREVENTION ACT - Merkley

content.text:
1) Answer

The clearest way to test whether a lawmaker “values human rights” is to check whether they repeatedly invest political capital in concrete, rights‑focused actions that become law and are enforced. Marco Rubio has done so, across multiple regions and years:

- He wrote and introduced the Uyghur Human Rights Policy Act of 2020; it passed Congress with overwhelming bipartisan support and was signed into law on June 17, 2020. The statute mandates U.S. government reporting and sanctions responses to abuses against Uyghurs in Xinjiang. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/senate-bill/3744/actions?utm_source=openai))

- He wrote and introduced the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act of 2019; it became law on November 27, 2019, requiring annual U.S. reviews of Hong Kong’s autonomy and authorizing sanctions for rights abuses. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/senate-bill/1838/amendments?utm_source=openai))

- He led the Senate version of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (S.65) in 2021; the final measure (H.R.6256) became Public Law 117‑78 on December 23, 2021, creating a rebuttable presumption that goods from Xinjiang are made with forced labor and blocking them at U.S. ports. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117-congress/senate-bill/65?utm_source=openai))

- He was an original cosponsor of the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act, the modern U.S. framework for sanctioning foreign human‑rights abusers and corrupt actors worldwide. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/114th-congress/senate-bill/284/all-info?utm_source=openai))

- He sponsored the Venezuela Defense of Human Rights and Civil Society Extension Act of 2016, extending mandatory U.S. sanctions authorities against Venezuelan officials responsible for human‑rights violations; it became Public Law 114‑194. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/114th-congress/senate-bill/2845?utm_source=openai))

- He served in leadership on the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional‑Executive Commission on China (CECC), which documents abuses and recommends U.S. policy responses; as cochair, he helped release the CECC’s 2020 Annual Report calling for concrete U.S. actions to address PRC abuses. ([cecc.gov](https://www.cecc.gov/media-center/press-releases/cecc-commissioners-release-2020-annual-report?utm_source=openai))

Taken together—drafting and passing multiple human‑rights laws that impose sanctions and trade consequences on abusers, and leading congressional oversight focused on human rights—this is strong, observable evidence that Rubio consistently values and advances human rights as a matter of U.S. policy.
